key_insight: The paper shows that conventional FPV can decouple flamelet state from the local strain environment, while an ε-based flamelet coupling restores a more strain-rate-consistent non-premixed combustion model.
engineering_relevance: For RANS combustion modeling, the ε-Z approach may improve prediction of quenching, product persistence, and flame response in high-strain transonic mixing layers.
method: 2D RANS simulations of a transonic accelerating reacting mixing layer
Compared one-step kinetics, conventional FPV, and the proposed ε-Z flamelet model
Used turbulence dissipation rate ε to infer flamelet strain rate S* and constrain tabulated chemistry
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a numerical evaluation showing that FPV preferentially samples near-equilibrium flamelet states in high-strain regions, whereas the ε-Z formulation maintains a tighter link between the flow field and flamelet response.
watch_item: Because the ε-Z model relies on inferred strain rate and pressure-dependent flammability limits, its accuracy may depend on the turbulence closure and the validity of the tabulated flamelet manifold under off-manifold conditions.
